log_one_plus_le_quintic: log(1+x) ≤ x - x²/2 + x³/3 - x⁴/4 + x⁵/5 for x > 0. Proof via derivative monotonicity: g(t) = polynomial - log(1+t), g'(t) = t⁵/(1+t) ≥ 0, g(0) = 0. Fifth-order alternating series upper bound — pairs with the existing fourth-order lower bound log_one_plus_ge_quartic to sandwich log(1+x) between consecutive-order polynomials. This is the next-order log infrastructure flagged in the prior session's nextSteps[0] ("second correction 1/(288n²): one additional log-bound order needed").

Geometric-series identity: 1 - t + t² - t³ + t⁴ = (1+t⁵)/(1+t). General pattern: Σ_{j=0}^{m-1} (-t)^j = (1 - (-t)^m)/(1+t), so the m-term partial sum's deviation from 1/(1+t) is exactly ±t^m/(1+t). This drives all the log_one_plus_{le,ge}_*ic bounds at every order, and is what powers the infinite tower of Stirling correction terms.
nextSteps: Second correction 1/(288n²): use log_one_plus_le_quintic + a paired sextic lower bound (log(1+x) ≥ x - x²/2 + x³/3 - x⁴/4 + x⁵/5 - x⁶/6) to derive a tighter step bound d_k = (1/(12k²)) + (1/(120k⁴)) + lower-order tails. This gives a two-term partial sum and ultimately |stirlingSeq(n)/√π - (1 + 1/(12n) + 1/(288n²))| ≤ C/n³.
